en: The Vajraśekhara Sūtra: The Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu;
the Dharma-body of the Self-Enjoyment Body of the Tathāgata Vairocana, consisting of the assembly of internally realized wisdom;
the Supreme Vehicle of the Buddhas’ Secret Samādhi.

The Liturgical Text for Repentance. Translated by Imperial Decree by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery—Great Master of Universal Wisdom (Dàguǎngzhì), posthumously titled Great Mirror (Dàjiàn), with the honorific title of Minister of Works (Sīkōng), invested as Duke of Sù with a fief of three thousand households, granted purple robes, and holding the rank of *Kaifù Yítóng sānsī* and *Tèjìn Shì Hónglú qīng*.
First, the Invocation and Praise of the Buddha according to the usual ritual: *Namo* to the eternally abiding, pure and wondrous Dharmakāya, the Vajradhātu, the Great Compassionate Vairocana Buddha.
“Homage to Akṣobhya Buddha, the body of the vajra-like firm intrinsic nature.
Homage to Ratnasambhava Buddha, the body of the accumulation of merit and adornment.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha, the body of the enjoyment of wisdom.”
"Homage to the Buddha Amoghasiddhi, who manifests through transformation bodies.

Homage to all Buddhas, including the Great Mirror-like Wisdom, the Vajra Perfection, those born from the Perfection that fills all lands within the dust motes of the Dharma-realm throughout the entirety of space, and so forth."

Homage to all Buddhas, who have arisen from the Jewel Pāramitā of the Wisdom of Equality and the Pāramitā of pervading the dust-motes of all lands throughout the entirety of empty space and the Dharma-realm.

Homage to all Buddhas, who arise from the perfection of the Dharma through the wisdom of wondrous discernment, and who extend throughout the entirety of space and the dharma-realm, reaching every atom and land.

Homage to all Buddhas who arise from the wisdom of accomplishment, the perfection of action (*karmapāramitā*), and the perfection that reaches as far as the reaches of space and pervades the dust-motes of the entire dharma-realm.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, the Bodhicitta-Vajrasattvas, and all Buddhas born from the Vajradhātu, who share a single essential nature throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, the Bodhicitta-Vajrarāja, and all Buddhas who arise from the Vajradhātu, whose single essential nature pervades the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, the Bodhicitta-vajra-love and others, who are of one identical nature throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, born from the Vajradhātu, all Buddhas.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, to the Bodhicitta-vajra-ānanda and others, whose single essential nature pervades the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, and who are born from the Vajradhātu—the bodies of all Buddhas.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, the mass of merit, the vajra-jewel, and so forth, who are of one identical nature throughout the entirety of space and the dharma-realm, born from the Vajradhātu, all Buddhas of the emanation body.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, the mass of merit, the vajra-light, and so forth—those who, throughout the entirety of space and the pervasiveness of the dharma-realm, are of one identical nature, the Vajradhātu-born bodies of all Buddhas.

Homage to all Buddhas who are the accumulation of merit of all Tathāgatas, the Vajradhvaja, and so forth—those whose single essential nature pervades the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, born from the vajra-realm, and who possess the bodies of all Buddhas.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, the mass of merit, Vajra-laughter, and so forth—those who are of one identical nature throughout the entirety of space and the pervasiveness of the Dharma-realm, born from the Vajradhātu, all Buddhas.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, the gateways of wisdom, the vajra-dharma-equality that pervades the entirety of space and the dharma-realm, whose single essential nature gives rise to the vajra-realm bodies of all Buddhas.
Homage to all Buddhas who arise from the Vajra Realm, whose single essential nature pervades the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, such as the Vajratīkṣṇa-gate of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.

Homage to all Buddhas, the embodiments born from the Vajra Realm, who possess a single essential nature pervading the Dharma-realm and filling the void of space, whose vajra causes are the gateways to the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.

Homage to all Buddhas, the vajra-born bodies who are of one single essence throughout the expanse of space and the reaches of the dharma-realm, whose vajra speech is the gateway to the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, the Greatly Valiant Ones, the Vajra-Action Ones, and so forth—those whose single essential nature pervades the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, the Vajra-born bodies of all Buddhas.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, the Greatly Valiant Vajra Protectors and others, whose single essential nature pervades the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, the Vajra-born bodies of all Buddhas.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, the Greatly Valiant Vajra-Teeth, whose single essential nature pervades the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, the Vajra-born bodies of all Buddhas.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, the Greatly Valiant Vajra-fists and others, whose single essential nature pervades the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, the Vajra-born bodies of all Buddhas.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas such as Sarvatathāgatapriyadarśanavajralāsyā and others, who fill the entirety of space and pervade the Dharma-realm, and to the ocean-like clouds of all offerings.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, to the Great Enlightenment-Portion Vajramālā and all others, and to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who are oceans of clouds of offerings, pervading the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the ocean-like clouds of offerings that pervade the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, such as the Wondrous Dharma-Sound Vajra Song.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, and to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas of the ocean-like clouds of offerings, such as the Vajra Dance of the Supernatural Powers and Activities of All Tathāgatas, which pervade the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, to the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who are like clouds and oceans of all offerings—such as the incense of the adamantine perfuming of True Suchness—that pervade the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, the Victorious Adornments, the Vajra Flowers, and so forth—to the ocean-like clouds of all offerings that pervade the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, and to the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and others.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, and to the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas such as the Constantly All-Illuminating Vajra Lamp, who fill the entirety of space and pervade the Dharma-realm like an ocean of clouds of offerings.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, and to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas such as the Ever-Offering Vajra-Perfume and others, who are like an ocean of clouds of offerings pervading the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who accomplish all things throughout the entirety of space and the pervasiveness of the Dharma-realm, such as the Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa of the Wisdom of the Four Means of Gathering.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, to the Bodhisattva Skillful Wisdom Vajra Lasso and all other Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who carry out instructions throughout the entirety of space and the pervasiveness of the Dharma-realm.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas such as Dṛḍhamati-vajraśṛṅkhalā, and to all the messenger Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who pervade the entirety of space and the dharma-realm.

Homage to all Tathāgatas, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas such as Joyful Wisdom Vajra Bell, and to all Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas who accord with the Dharma throughout the entirety of space and the pervasiveness of the Dharmadhātu.
As described above, the thirty-seven deities of the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu are all the inner retinue of the Dharma-Buddha’s realization of bodhi, and are the mutual embodiments of Vairocana.

Homage to the Three Jewels, who eternally abide in equality throughout the three periods of time within the assembly of unspeakably unspeakable oceans of lands, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable oceans of worlds within the Lotus Treasury World-Ocean throughout the ten directions.
Universally for the five classes:

the celestial lords of the world, the transcendent parents of the nine directions, all spiritual friends, the donors of the site of enlightenment, and all sentient beings throughout the realms without exception—may they together vow to sever all hindrances and take refuge through repentance. With a sincere heart, they repent:
"Throughout the beginningless cycle of existence within the various realms, The offenses produced by the actions of body, speech, and mind..."
"Just as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have performed repentance, so do I now present my confession.
Having finished the repentance, with a sincere heart take refuge in and pay homage to the Great Compassionate Vairocana Buddha; with a sincere heart rejoice:
"Furthermore, one should deeply give rise to a joyful mind and rejoice in all accumulations of merit and wisdom."
Within the practices and vows of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, I rejoice in all the merit produced by the three vajra activities,
as well as in all the roots of goodness accumulated by Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and all sentient beings.
Having rejoiced, they take refuge with a sincere heart and prostrate to the Great Compassionate Vairocana Buddha, making this earnest entreaty:
"Beholding again all Buddhas seated beneath the Bodhi tree, Each one personally requests them to turn the Wheel of Dharma;
All Lamps of the World, seated at the site of enlightenment, Open the eyes of awakening to illuminate the three realms of existence."
To all the Tathāgatas, lords of the three realms, who are about to enter parinirvāṇa without remainder,
I entreat them all to remain for a long time, not forsaking their compassionate vows to save the world.
Having made this exhortation, one should take refuge with a sincere heart and prostrate to the Great Compassionate Vairocana Buddha, dedicating the merit with a sincere heart:
"Through the merit of repentance, sympathetic joy, and exhortation, May I never lose the bodhicitta;
Amidst the wondrous assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, May I always be a virtuous friend, never wearying or abandoning them."
Far removed from the eight difficulties, one is born where there are no obstacles; With the wisdom of recollecting past lives, the marks adorn the body;
Free from delusion and endowed with compassion and wisdom, One is able to fully fulfill all the pāramitās.
May they be born into noble families with abundant wealth and prosperity, With vast retinues that are ever flourishing,
Possessing the four unhindered analytical knowledges and the ten masteries, And fully perfecting the six supernormal powers and all meditative absorptions—
Just as with Vajradhvaja and Samantabhadra, May my praise and dedication likewise be so.

Having completed the dedication and the making of vows, and having with a sincere heart taken refuge in and prostrated before the Great Compassionate Buddha Vairocana, proceed next in the usual sequence.
Address the assembly, and each should recite this verse of purity for the present moment:
"All phenomena are like reflections, Pure and free from all defilement."
"Grasping and speech are unobtainable; All arise from causes and karma.

*The Liturgical Text for Prostration and Repentance of the Vajraśekhara Sūtra, the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu, the Self-Enjoyment Body of the Tathāgata Vairocana, the Inner Realization Wisdom Retinue, the Dharma Body under Alternative Names of the Buddha, the Supreme Vehicle Secret Samādhi; also known as the Liturgical Text for Prostration and Repentance of the Thirty-Seven Honored Ones.*
